cd c:/Dev/rore/Pallium && git commit -m "PR 0 step 3: Tier A shape expansion + Tier B entropy+context redaction

Motivation (2026-07-02 live audit): the shared redaction helper covered
Bearer [REDACTED] X-API-Key + env-var KVs + PEM blocks + connection strings.
The live DB carried unredacted Slack (xoxb-/xoxp-), GitHub PAT (ghp_),
env-secret KVs, and one JDBC connection string across ~77 memory rows
each and 5 lexical_fts index entries — retrievable by any query hitting
them. Root cause: the helper had no coverage for provider-shaped tokens.

semantic/redaction.py expansion:

Tier A (provider-specific regexes, most-specific-prefix-first):
- GitHub PAT/OAuth/user/server/refresh: \\b(gh[pousr])_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,255}\\b
- Slack bot/user/app strict + legacy fallback shapes
- Anthropic sk-ant-, OpenAI sk-proj-, generic sk- (order-safe)
- AWS AKIA + ASIA (STS session credentials)
- JWT triple with URL-safe base64
- Basic-auth URL user:pass@ — preserves scheme + host
- Broadened env-var name set: APIKEY, APITOKEN, PAT, CREDENTIALS,
  PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, REFRESH_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET
- New yaml-separator env-var rule: password: value (case-insensitive)

Tier B (redact_probable_secrets):
Runs after Tier A. Any \\W-boundaried run of [A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-.]{20,}
whose Shannon entropy ≥ 4.0 bits/char AND that sits within 30 chars of
a secret-cue word (password/token/secret/auth/bearer/credential/etc.)
gets replaced with [REDACTED-Nc] where N is the token length. FP
guards short-circuit before entropy compute:
- Git commit SHAs (40 hex chars)
- UUIDs
- Content-addressed hashes (32-64 hex)
Deliberate exclusions from cue-word list: 'key' alone (FP on
'keyboard shortcut', 'primary key'). Compound forms api_key /
access_key / private_key are included instead.
= is excluded from the token character class so NAME=value strings
stay separable into name (checked by the cue-word window) and value.

Idempotence: redact_sensitive(redact_sensitive(x)) == redact_sensitive(x).
Tier A replaces with [REDACTED] (opaque, no size); Tier B uses
[REDACTED-Nc] (retains length signal for post-hoc analysis). Neither
marker's characters overlap the Tier B token character class, so a
second pass produces no new matches.

Bounded worst case: Tier B skips inputs > 1,000,000 chars to bound
per-write cost. All Tier A regexes have explicit upper quantifier
bounds to prevent catastrophic backtracking on hostile input.

Tests: tests/test_redaction_tier_a_and_b.py — 58 cases covering:
- Every Tier A shape with a realistic token
- Ordering (sk-ant- must not be downgraded to generic sk-)
- Tier B cue-word matrix (parametrized over the full cue-word set)
- Tier B FP guards for git SHAs, UUIDs, content hashes
- Tier B without cue word — not redacted
- Idempotence + marker-not-re-matched
- Empty / very long / multi-secret / adjacent / start / end / binary bytes
- Tier A wins over Tier B (marker style asserted)
- MYPASSWORD / HOTKEY word-boundary FP guards preserved
- Pre-existing pin: Bearer, X-API-Key, PEM block, Authorization header
  behaviors unchanged

Test plan:
python -m pytest tests/test_redaction_tier_a_and_b.py -q      # 58 pass
python -m pytest tests/test_redaction.py -q                    # PR-A tests still green (43 pass)
python -m pytest tests/ -q                                     # 3221 pass, no regression

Next in PR 0: FTS-safe redact_index_entry_text_view helper, universal
write barrier at core/service.py::ingest_item, wire LLM-extraction paths,
retrieval barrier, secrets_purge CLI, e2e tests 10a/10b. See plan file
noble-brewing-squid.md for the full sequence." 2>&1 | tail -6

Motivation (2026-07-02 live audit): the shared redaction helper covered
Bearer [REDACTED] X-API-Key + env-var KVs + PEM blocks + connection strings.
The live DB carried unredacted Slack (xoxb-/xoxp-), GitHub PAT (ghp_),
env-secret KVs, and one JDBC connection string across ~77 memory rows
each and 5 lexical_fts index entries — retrievable by any query hitting
them. Root cause: the helper had no coverage for provider-shaped tokens.

semantic/redaction.py expansion:

Tier A (provider-specific regexes, most-specific-prefix-first):
- GitHub PAT/OAuth/user/server/refresh: \\b(gh[pousr])_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,255}\\b
- Slack bot/user/app strict + legacy fallback shapes
- Anthropic sk-ant-, OpenAI sk-proj-, generic sk- (order-safe)
- AWS AKIA + ASIA (STS session credentials)
- JWT triple with URL-safe base64
- Basic-auth URL user:pass@ — preserves scheme + host
- Broadened env-var name set: APIKEY, APITOKEN, PAT, CREDENTIALS,
  PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, REFRESH_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET
- New yaml-separator env-var rule: password: value (case-insensitive)

Tier B (redact_probable_secrets):
Runs after Tier A. Any \\W-boundaried run of [A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-.]{20,}
whose Shannon entropy ≥ 4.0 bits/char AND that sits within 30 chars of
a secret-cue word (password/token/secret/auth/bearer/credential/etc.)
gets replaced with [REDACTED-Nc] where N is the token length. FP
guards short-circuit before entropy compute:
- Git commit SHAs (40 hex chars)
- UUIDs
- Content-addressed hashes (32-64 hex)
Deliberate exclusions from cue-word list: 'key' alone (FP on
'keyboard shortcut', 'primary key'). Compound forms api_key /
access_key / private_key are included instead.
= is excluded from the token character class so NAME=value strings
stay separable into name (checked by the cue-word window) and value.

Idempotence: redact_sensitive(redact_sensitive(x)) == redact_sensitive(x).
Tier A replaces with [REDACTED] (opaque, no size); Tier B uses
[REDACTED-Nc] (retains length signal for post-hoc analysis). Neither
marker's characters overlap the Tier B token character class, so a
second pass produces no new matches.

Bounded worst case: Tier B skips inputs > 1,000,000 chars to bound
per-write cost. All Tier A regexes have explicit upper quantifier
bounds to prevent catastrophic backtracking on hostile input.

- Tier B cue-word matrix (parametrized over the full cue-word set)
- Tier B FP guards for git SHAs, UUIDs, content hashes
- Tier B without cue word — not redacted
- Idempotence + marker-not-re-matched
- Empty / very long / multi-secret / adjacent / start / end / binary bytes
- Tier A wins over Tier B (marker style asserted)
- MYPASSWORD / HOTKEY word-boundary FP guards preserved
- Pre-existing pin: Bearer, X-API-Key, PEM block, Authorization header
  behaviors unchanged

Motivation (2026-07-02 live audit): the shared redaction helper covered
Bearer [REDACTED] X-API-Key + env-var KVs + PEM blocks + connection strings.
The live DB carried unredacted Slack (xoxb-/xoxp-), GitHub PAT (ghp_),
env-secret KVs, and one JDBC connection string across ~77 memory rows
each and 5 lexical_fts index entries — retrievable by any query hitting
them. Root cause: the helper had no coverage for provider-shaped tokens.

semantic/redaction.py expansion:

Tier A (provider-specific regexes, most-specific-prefix-first):
- GitHub PAT/OAuth/user/server/refresh: \\b(gh[pousr])_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,255}\\b
- Slack bot/user/app strict + legacy fallback shapes
- Anthropic sk-ant-, OpenAI sk-proj-, generic sk- (order-safe)
- AWS AKIA + ASIA (STS session credentials)
- JWT triple with URL-safe base64
- Basic-auth URL user:pass@ — preserves scheme + host
- Broadened env-var name set: APIKEY, APITOKEN, PAT, CREDENTIALS,
  PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, REFRESH_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET
- New yaml-separator env-var rule: password: value (case-insensitive)

Tier B (redact_probable_secrets):
Runs after Tier A. Any \\W-boundaried run of [A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-.]{20,}
whose Shannon entropy ≥ 4.0 bits/char AND that sits within 30 chars of
a secret-cue word (password/token/secret/auth/bearer/credential/etc.)
gets replaced with [REDACTED-Nc] where N is the token length. FP
guards short-circuit before entropy compute:
- Git commit SHAs (40 hex chars)
- UUIDs
- Content-addressed hashes (32-64 hex)
Deliberate exclusions from cue-word list: 'key' alone (FP on
'keyboard shortcut', 'primary key'). Compound forms api_key /
access_key / private_key are included instead.
= is excluded from the token character class so NAME=value strings
stay separable into name (checked by the cue-word window) and value.

Idempotence: redact_sensitive(redact_sensitive(x)) == redact_sensitive(x).
Tier A replaces with [REDACTED] (opaque, no size); Tier B uses
[REDACTED-Nc] (retains length signal for post-hoc analysis). Neither
marker's characters overlap the Tier B token character class, so a
second pass produces no new matches.

Bounded worst case: Tier B skips inputs > 1,000,000 chars to bound
per-write cost. All Tier A regexes have explicit upper quantifier
bounds to prevent catastrophic backtracking on hostile input.

semantic/redaction.py expansion:

Tier A (provider-specific regexes, most-specific-prefix-first):
- GitHub PAT/OAuth/user/server/refresh: \\b(gh[pousr])_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,255}\\b
- Slack bot/user/app strict + legacy fallback shapes
- Anthropic sk-ant-, OpenAI sk-proj-, generic sk- (order-safe)
- AWS AKIA + ASIA (STS session credentials)
- JWT triple with URL-safe base64
- Basic-auth URL user:pass@ — preserves scheme + host

  PRIVATE_KEY, SIGNING_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, REFRESH_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET

Tier B (redact_probable_secrets):
Runs after Tier A. Any \\W-boundaried run of [A-Za-z0-9+/_\\-.]{20,}
whose Shannon entropy ≥ 4.0 bits/char AND that sits within 30 chars of
a secret-cue word (password/token/secret/auth/bearer/credential/etc.)
gets replaced with [REDACTED-Nc] where N is the token length. FP
guards short-circuit before entropy compute:
- Git commit SHAs (40 hex chars)
- UUIDs
- Content-addressed hashes (32-64 hex)

'keyboard shortcut', 'primary key'). Compound forms api_key /
access_key / private_key are included instead.
= is excluded from the token character class so NAME=value strings
stay separable into name (checked by the cue-word window) and value.

Idempotence: redact_sensitive(redact_sensitive(x)) == redact_sensitive(x).

[REDACTED-Nc] (retains length signal for post-hoc analysis). Neither
marker's characters overlap the Tier B token character class, so a
second pass produces no new matches.

bounds to prevent catastrophic backtracking on hostile input.

   (and note) store their human-facing text under payload.subject.

   subject column is NULL for older rows written before the subject-
   writer landed.

   truncated. Types that don't carry confidence (task_trace,
   operational_fact) should not display noise.

  Any type that stores its summary under payload.subject (currently
  operational_fact, and note as of W3) now surfaces cleanly.

  core.subject.subject_text_for_payload when the column is NULL.
  display_text falls back to the derived subject when the payload
  has no dedicated summary key.

  the literal 'unknown' string. High/medium/low chips unaffected.

commands.cmd:
cd c:/Dev/rore/Pallium && git add -A && git commit -m "fix(dashboard): render operational_fact + note subject; hide 'unknown' confidence

Live dashboard was showing 12 operational_fact rows as '<no summary>'
with a noisy 'unkno…' Conf chip because:

1. _DISPLAY_TEXT_KEYS did not include 'subject' — operational_fact
   (and note) store their human-facing text under payload.subject.
2. The endpoint emitted rec.subject directly, but the memory_objects
   subject column is NULL for older rows written before the subject-
   writer landed.
3. The Conf column rendered 'unknown' literally, producing 'unkno…'
   truncated. Types that don't carry confidence (task_trace,
   operational_fact) should not display noise.

## Changes

- storage/sqlite.py: _DISPLAY_TEXT_KEYS gains 'subject' at the tail.
  Any type that stores its summary under payload.subject (currently
  operational_fact, and note as of W3) now surfaces cleanly.
- app/dashboard.py: dashboard_memories endpoint falls back to
  core.subject.subject_text_for_payload when the column is NULL.
  display_text falls back to the derived subject when the payload
  has no dedicated summary key.
- app/dashboard.html: Conf column renders '—' (em-dash) instead of
  the literal 'unknown' string. High/medium/low chips unaffected.

## Test coverage

- test_memories_operational_fact_renders_subject: seed an
  operational_fact and assert display_text + subject are populated
  (regression pin for the '<no summary>' defect).
- test_memories_subject_falls_back_when_column_null: force-null the
  subject column and assert the endpoint recovers via
  subject_text_for_payload.

## Verification

- pytest tests/test_dashboard.py -q -> 21 passed in 2.89s.
- pytest tests/ -q (deselecting pre-existing) -> 3047 passed, +2 new.
  Zero regressions.
